input_messages.content: Hi, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. The internet is either extremely slow or just stops working altogether. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone—nothing less will do. Can you help me fix this? I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my mobile data to work perfectly.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next to get my mobile data working at excellent speed.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed due to no connection. What should I do next to get my mobile data working?
My status bar shows that Airplane Mode is enabled, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or data icons like “4G”, “5G”, or “LTE.” What should I do next?
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, my status bar shows a poor signal, “2G,” and a “Data Disabled” icon. What should I do next? My mobile data still isn’t working.

I’ve turned on mobile data. The “Data Disabled” icon is gone, and now it shows “Data Enabled,” but I’m still only seeing “2G” with a poor signal. What should I do next? I really need excellent internet speed.

I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now my status bar shows an excellent signal, “5G,” and data is enabled. Should I try another speed test to check if the internet speed is excellent now?

I tried running the speed test again, but it still failed due to no connection, even though I have an excellent 5G signal and data is enabled. This is getting frustrating—what else can we try to actually get excellent internet speed?

I checked my APN settings, and the APN name is set to “internet” with the MMSC URL as “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” There don’t seem to be any errors or missing fields. What should I do next to get my mobile data working at excellent speed?
I definitely do not want to change my mobile data plan, but I am willing to add 2GB of data to my line. Please go ahead and refuel my data so I can get my internet working at excellent speed.

I tried running the speed test again after adding 2GB of data, but it still failed due to no connection. My mobile data is still not working, and I’m not getting the excellent internet speed I need. What else can we try?
I’ve restarted my phone. The status bar still shows an excellent 5G signal and data enabled. Should I try running the speed test again now?

I ran the speed test again after restarting my phone, but it still failed due to no connection. My mobile data is still not working, and I’m not getting any internet speed at all. What else can we do to actually fix this?
Yes, please transfer me to a human agent. I really need this fixed so I can get excellent internet speed on my phone. Thank you.

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

# User Simulation Guidelines
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. The internet is either extremely slow or just stops working altogether. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone—nothing less will do. Can you help me fix this? I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my mobile data to work perfectly.

To help you with your mobile data issue, I’ll need to identify your account first. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can begin troubleshooting your mobile data problem.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know what you need me to do next to get my mobile data working at excellent speed.

Thank you for providing your information. To begin troubleshooting your mobile data issue and help you achieve excellent speed, I’ll need you to perform a quick speed test on your phone. This will help us determine the current quality of your mobile data connection.

Please run a speed test on your device and let me know the result. If you need instructions on how to do this, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed due to no connection. What should I do next to get my mobile data working?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your speed test failed due to no connection, let’s start by checking your phone’s basic connectivity status. Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:

- Do you see any signal bars, or does it show “No Signal”?
- Is Airplane Mode enabled?
- Do you see any icons like “4G”, “5G”, or “LTE” at the top of your screen?
- Is there a “Data Disabled” or similar icon?

This information will help me determine the next steps to restore your mobile data connection.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
My status bar shows that Airplane Mode is enabled, and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or data icons like “4G”, “5G”, or “LTE.” What should I do next?

Your phone’s Airplane Mode is currently enabled, which turns off all wireless connections—including mobile data and cellular service. To restore your mobile data connection, please turn off Airplane Mode on your device.

Once you have turned off Airplane Mode, check if your signal bars and data icons (like “4G” or “5G”) reappear. Let me know what you see after disabling Airplane Mode, and if your mobile data starts working. If not, we’ll continue troubleshooting.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now, my status bar shows a poor signal, “2G,” and a “Data Disabled” icon. What should I do next? My mobile data still isn’t working.

Thank you for the update. Here’s what we need to address next:

1. Your phone is connected to a “2G” network, which is too slow for modern internet use.
2. Mobile data is currently disabled.

Let’s start by enabling your mobile data. Please turn on mobile data in your phone’s settings. Once you’ve done that, let me know if the “Data Disabled” icon disappears and if you see any data icons like “4G” or “5G.” If your phone still shows “2G,” we’ll proceed to update your network mode for better speed.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve turned on mobile data. The “Data Disabled” icon is gone, and now it shows “Data Enabled,” but I’m still only seeing “2G” with a poor signal. What should I do next? I really need excellent internet speed.

Since your phone is still connected to a “2G” network, which is not suitable for high-speed internet, the next step is to change your network mode preference to allow 4G or 5G connections.

Please go to your phone’s network settings and set the preferred network mode to “4G/5G preferred” (sometimes labeled as “LTE/5G” or “Auto”). After changing this setting, check your status bar to see if it connects to a faster network like “4G” or “5G” and if your signal improves.

Let me know what network type appears after you update this setting, and if your mobile data speed improves. If you still have issues, we’ll continue troubleshooting.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now my status bar shows an excellent signal, “5G,” and data is enabled. Should I try another speed test to check if the internet speed is excellent now?

Yes, please run another speed test now that your phone is connected to “5G” with an excellent signal and data enabled. This will help confirm if your internet speed meets your needs.

Let me know the result of the speed test. If the speed is still not excellent, we can continue troubleshooting further.
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I tried running the speed test again, but it still failed due to no connection, even though I have an excellent 5G signal and data is enabled. This is getting frustrating—what else can we try to actually get excellent internet speed?

Thank you for your patience. Since you have an excellent 5G signal and data is enabled, but still cannot connect to the internet, the issue may be related to your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for mobile data to work.

The next step is to check your APN settings. Please check your phone’s APN settings and let me know if you see any errors or if the APN/MMSC fields are empty or incorrect. If you’re unsure how to check this, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you.

If the APN settings are incorrect or missing, you’ll need to reset them to default and then reboot your device. Let me know what you find, and I’ll walk you through the next steps.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and the APN name is set to “internet” with the MMSC URL as “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” There don’t seem to be any errors or missing fields. What should I do next to get my mobile data working at excellent speed?
